item.title: An in-universe parody of Are We Cool Yet.
item.description: Are We Cool Yet? No, we're pretentious wankers.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

-Anomalous statue with "Are We Cool Yet" carved into the bottom. Occasionally 'activates', creating a memetic aura causing a variety of effects in people around them. Note attached, filled with nonsensical writing "explaining" the artistic significance of the statue. The effects are assumed by the Foundation to be some kind of pretentious commentary, as most AWCY projects are, and try to figure out what it all means in an attempt to stop its effects or discover its creator.

-Is eventually revealed to be an in-universe parody of AWCY, likely made by a member of ACWY as a sort of self-own after it stops its effects and is reclassified as neutralised.

Central Narrative:

-Foundation attempts to interpret the effects of the statue, researching increasingly obscure art pieces and reaching more and more in an attempt to work out what the artist was trying to say.

-One of the statues effects makes the researchers think the statue is prophesying some catastrophic event, fuelled by their own (justified, at this point) paranoia, and begin kidnapping and interrogating AWCY members to no avail.

+ show block
– hide block

-Their interpretations become ridiculously complex in a search for some kind of cohesive meaning, matching the actual effects of the statue becoming more nonsensical and racking up a larger body count in the process. Eventually the statue starts just killing people at random for seemingly no reason, before stopping completely.

-Item is reclassified as "Safe" or "neutralized" and the foundation eventually works out that they have inadvertently been led on a wild goose chase, and deduce the item was meant as a parody of AWCY themselves- meaningless effects resulting in unnecessarily deaths and a note pretentiously explaining the work.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

-The items effects are extremely weird and nonsensical, and the foundation's interpretations of the items effects cross-link other SCP's and reference various societal or historical events, phenomenon, and art pieces.

-As far as I could tell there aren't any AWCY scips that directly make fun of their own group, which seems something right up their alley.

Additional Notes:

-Started as a GAW project, but I prefer it as an actual AWCY member making fun of the group he's apart of.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: The Price Of Greed
item.description: SEEKING GREENLIGHT: An SCP article about a watch that everyone wants, and makes them a monster if they have it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Genre (Optional): Cautionary Tale

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

SCP-XXXX is an old, worn-down wrist watch. It's anomalous effect causes anyone who has seen or heard about the watch, either in person or in some form of media, to seek it out and steal it by any means necessary. Once in possession of the watch an individual will become unnaturally violent and aggressive, especially to others that want to take the watch for themselves.

+ Central Narrative
- Close

The central narrative revolves around the Foundation's difficulty in containing the object because the greed it causes is unending. It begins with the item's initial recovery, where after an incident in which a police officer killed a civilian during a routine traffic stop because he wanted to steal the watch, which the civilian was wearing.

After stealing the watch the officer is beaten to death and the watch is once again stolen. The foundation tracks down this individual due to reports of anomalous activity. During the investigation more casualties occur as the man and two Foundation Officers are killed due to the influence of the SCP-XXXX. After this point, the watch is finally taken into foundation custody.

This series of events would be told through an interview log with the Team Captain and an audio log taken from the police database. Afterward, some test logs will reveal the extent of the watches' influence on people and the kind of powers that it has. An addendum from the site director will issue an order for all records of the watch to be destroyed, and for a mass amnestic to be administered to all personnel assigned to the object due to the extreme effects it has on the human psyche. He will also issue a manhunt for the lead researcher as they have gone AWOL and stolen the watch, leaving more dead in the wake of greed.

+ Hook/Attention-Grabber
- Close

The hook of the story will be that as the article goes on it is revealed that the watch has the secondary effect of causing people who are in possession of the watch to be viewed as a literal monster or something to be threatened by.

For example a foundation agent might view someone wearing the watch as if they looked like SCP-682. This would cause the agent to lash out in fear, possibly killing the watch-bearer, and then steal the watch due to its primary influence. Thus ensuring that the cycle of greed will repeat again.

item.title: Data not redacted? (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Something or someone is censoring information on foundation database and its spreading.
item.content:encoded:
Something or someone is censoring information on foundation database with ████ or [DATA REDACTED] and it is spreading to all known copies including pyhsical ones.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Classic article with table wizard and dialogs

Elevator Pitch: Basic idea is that something is "corrupting" Foundation database with random censors like ████ or [DATA REDACTED] while the censored information was currently known before and cant be find anywhere including any copies of it. This phenomenon (due to unknown nature SCP-XXXX supposed to be phenomenon for now) is somehow spreading to other articles. You may think that hey maybe thats just normal its some kind of error or GoI spies right? (And no its not, with some logical response. I can explain it if its needed in comments)

Central Narrative: It gives several theories and hypothesis about whats the reason or whats the behind it, is it some sort of entity or GoI spies? Also discovery of it by junior researcher and going to foundation web crawlers one by one to discover it. However this is just a discovery, initial censor that caused by SCP-XXXX might be the source of its spread but it can also not be and might led to much deeper origins.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: So we know that somehow SCP-XXXX corrupts database but how we can be sure that SCP-XXXX didnt corrupt this article. (Lets call it Article A) Answer is simple but effective. If there is any censor in article there must be a explanation for it.

For example: Then solution is [DATA REDACTED] (It has been censored due to being possible cognitohazard.)

So by using this method exclusively for our Article A we can be sure that Article A is not corrupted and safe to read.

Addendum: I already wrote it on sandbox because i didnt know i had to greenlight before posting to draft forums. In the last part of the sandbox there is a message that concludes that it might be all Ethics Comittee doing it for gaining upperhand against the O-5's so they actually created this supposed SCP (Since they also know every single censored line wrote in Ethics Comittee Orientation). However this sounded a bit extreme especially for first time writing and it kinda removes the mystery out of it. So i am very skeptical about that part.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Mirror Cyborgs
item.description: an android doppelganger tries to assasinate the human it is a copy of
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Science Fiction

Page Layout: Standard SCP article

Elevator Pitch: A pair of cyborgs that appear to be identical and one is trying to assassinate and replace the other. One is just a human with a Gyrfalcon series prosthetic arm, the assassin is an android(Saker, Peregrine, or something in between) with the flesh and blood arm of its target. The human knows nothing of the origin of the android, especially how it got the arm that shouldn't even still be intact. When Anderson Robotics is investigated, even they don't know where the doppelganger came from nor do they have any records of it's construction.

Central Narrative: The android claims to originate from SCP-3560 and implies that all Gyrfalcon prosthetics are actually powered by inhabitants of that dimension which are partially dismantled by Anderson's anomalous construction process. This one regenerated the limb from it's human counterpart and escaped, though how remains a mystery. But it definitely must be contained for futher interrogation and to prevent it from killing it's target. The target has proven to be relatively innocent and agreed to work for the Foundation as a double agent in the Church of Maxwell.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For every Gyrfalcon, there is a cybernetic doppelganger hunting down the human user, this is just the only one they found so far.

Additional Notes: I'm currently working under the theory that the true power behind Anderson Robotics is the Broken God which has allowed Anderson to build his army, but Anderson has gotten greedy and thinks he can claim the power for himself, and his recent turn of fate is the Broken God getting even with him. SCP-3560 was mentioned to have predated Anderson in a footnote in SCP-4000, I am assuming that rather than simply being an afterlife for the robots, it's more of in between lives, that they existed before and every time Anderson creates a new robot, it's a copy of an existing soul and the all the tech has been reverse engineered from the ancient army of Wan.

item.title: The Hourglass concept
item.description: This is my concept on a possible upcoming SCP of mine. I am looking forward to improving on this, since this is my first SCP entry.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre : Horror

Elevator Pitch: The Hourglass is right now known as safe, unless its broken. Anomalous effects are given off of the hourglass if physically touched, or around it for a certain amount of time (part inspired by 053). The user will begin to feel an urge to break the hourglass. If the breakage is successful, 2 things have a chance of happening, like a 50/50. Either the universe will freeze in time upon breakage, or the user that broke the hourglass will have full control over the sands of time.

Central Narrative: This concept is to be a unique SCP, it would be safe while docile, but when the hourglass is broken, a universal threat comes into play. While this may not be the best choice, it would seem very interesting as a concept, like the proposal of SCP-001 by S.D Locke.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This concept, once triggered/activated, it will have full control over the universe, either transferring that power to the user that broke the hourglass, or freezing the universe entirely. Even if this were not to happen, it would still be a riot causing devastation within the foundation, and the universe.

Additional Notes: None.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Mirror Mirror
item.description: Seeking conceptual approval for my first attempt at a SCP article.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP-Article

Page Layout:
Item #:
Object Class:
Special Containment Procedure:
Description:
Addendum: (Record of all known cases of individuals coming into contact with SCP-5615)

Elevator Pitch:
*A reality warping Euclid object in the form of a large, full length ornate silver mirror. The glass of the mirror is jet black like a traditional Scrying mirror.

  • Was recovered from the city of Yakutsk, Russia. Mass spectrometry of the impurities in the silver shows it's likely place of origin somewhere near the Taryno-Kurdatsky silver mine.

*People in close proximity to the mirror are mimetically compelled to want to stare into the mirror.
*Any sentient non-anomalous entity that stares into the mirror will undergo transfiguration based on some internal quality, desire or fear. However, the quality used to guide this transfiguration seems to be random, or may be directed by some unobserved intelligence.

+ show block
– hide block

*Most transfiguration seem to be malicious in nature, however some notable exceptions have been observed.
*May be vaguely linked to SCP-352
*The transfiguration event seems to also happen to anyone that sees a live image of the mirror. Hence, SCP could possibly trigger a RK/CK-event if a live broadcast of it was ever made public.

Central Narrative: Expands the lore of SCP's with a strong connection to a specific countries (Russia)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Transfiguration based SCP's aren't terribly common on the wiki. Especially ones that aren't inherently detrimental. The Nature of the SCP also compels people to try and utilize it for good, however unlike most SCP's using D-class personnel to experiment with the effects of the mirror is ill advised, if not suicidal.

Additional Notes: I have little experience using HTML formatting and templates. So I am concerned that I may need help properly formatting my submission (assuming it gets past the green lighting phase).

item.title: Transfer consciousness to a non-physical entity
item.description: Seeking Greenlights, approval and feedback of my idea.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlights and approval of my idea.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a metallic cylinder formed object that is presumed to be a replica to sleeping pods. The object's dimensions reach approximately 2.5 meters in length, 1.3 meters in width and stands 1 meter tall. When the subject enters SCP-XXXX, and the capsule has been sealed, a colorless, odorless gas will continuously be released from the tubes located within SCP-XXXX, and the subject will fall asleep usually within 10-20 seconds. Subject's consciousness will then be transported to a non-physical entity right next to SCP-XXXX, classified as SCP-XXXX-1, where the subject has full control of SCP-XXXX-1. Subject within SCP-XXXX-1 remains undetectable from human observation, other organic life forms, cameras and UV-light. SCP-XXXX-1 has the ability to see, hear, lift objects and even break the laws of physics, for example, traversing through solid surfaces. Subject's consciousness returns to their physical body once awoken from their slumber, and is able to recall their experience within SCP-XXXX-1.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX's place of origin is located on the Gallipoli peninsula on Achi Baba, Turkey, and was discovered in 198X buried one or two meters underground. No sources have been found indicating its purpose on Achi Baba. Given the capsules functions, a hypothesis claims that the Ottoman army, would use SCP-XXXX to infiltrate allied lines to gather intelligence about defensive positions. It is reckoned that SCP-XXXX was buried due to heavy artillery and was left behind as allied forces marched forward a few days after. However, the hypothesis gives no explanation behind the fact that only one exists. The hypothesis has been discarded.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • The given "ghost" form (or SCP-XXXX-1) is capable of phasing through solid surfaces and remain undetectable for approximately 1 hour period of time.
  • SCP-XXXX can perhaps be used as a tool and contribute to personnel such as cleaning, for example, SCP-173's container without unnecessary casualties. This also goes for experiments that require close contact with hostile SCPs.
  • The colorless, odorless gas which is supposed to resemble anesthesia, can perhaps also be used as a tool against other SCPs to gain control or cease aggression.

Additional Notes: It is a huge contrast how SCP-XXXX-1 has the ability to break the laws of physics yet is able to pick up objects. I will try to combine non-fictional science and make a logical argument about this huge contrast, if my idea gets an approval.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight for Attention Seeking Dog
item.description: Seeking a Greenlight for SCP article
item.content:encoded:
SEEKING GREENLIGHTS
Yes!


TYPE OF ARTICLE

SCP Article


ELEVATOR PITCH


The mummified corpse of a dog that decreases the cognitive function of those in its vicinity. When directly viewed, the victim becomes "goofy" and playful, wanting to play with the SCP and expressing how cute the dog is in affectionate and childish ways.

Once a person has viewed the SCP, the effect never wears off, and will die of dehydration or starvation if left unattended.

If skeletal structure of the dog is damaged, it screams and any person actively engaging in harming it become inconsolably filled with dread and regret.

+ show block
– hide block

CENTRAL NARRATIVE


Initial testing showed that portions of skin could be removed from the SCP, and said skin would possess none of the anomalous qualities of the SCP. Scientists think that they may be able to neutralize the SCP by sectioning the SCP into parts, as portions separate from the main body do not possess anomalous qualities.

(Because it's a real pain because the radius of its effects are large enough to need a special isolated containment.)

The surgery fails and activates the previous unknown third effect, sending Dr. Wilsons, the surgeon operating the robotic surgical equipment, into a nervous breakdown. Foundation scientists, curious about this phenomenon, load the SCP into a hydraulic press and command a D-Class to activate it. That D-Class also suffers a mental breakdown and refuses to continue the test even after threats of termination.

HOOK

I want to write a story about a cognito-hazard that has the effects of making people effected by it complete idiots and completely in love with a "little doggy" when it actually is just a creepy emaciated corpse

item.title: Fourth Dimensional Autocomplete Device
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A USB device which is able to repair damaged files and documents. It can fully repair any document or picture given as little as a digitally scanned shred of paper. In addition, the device can predictively write documents which haven't been completed by their authors. So long as the device is given a title and author, it can predict what will be written with 100% accuracy. However, If the author reads the predicted document before finishing their work, they may write something different. The device also modifies cognitohazards in a manner that makes them safe to view.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The document is written after the device's initial containment and eventual containment breach. Testing the device has revealed it's potential to complete unfinished documents until the head researcher, Dr. Swartz, lazily types in a draft of the SCP article, hoping that the device will complete it for him. The device returns a completed SCP article about itself. In a mysterious test log which has not been conducted or scheduled, Dr. Swartz dies from a memetic kill agent repaired by SCP-XXXX. The test concludes with the suspension of all testing until an AI safety chip is attached to the device.

Knowing that he will not conduct the next test, Swartz inputs the same draft into the device. As Swartz learns more about potential futures, they change in his favor. Soon, one of the articles describes an interesting test. A cognitohazard which causes nausea and vomiting when viewed is run through the device. D-class personnel are forced to look at it, but don't experience any symptoms. The test is repeated with a memetic kill agent, which does not kill any of the D-Class.

Dr. Swartz realizes that the test in which he died could not possibly have happened the way the article said. The SCP is incapable of reproducing cognitohazards. Swartz will likely be assassinated due to the device's ability to give him classified information. He goes on to use the device to escape Site 15 and the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Upon containment, SCP-XXXX is to be stored in Site 15 secure storage under constant surveillance. Anybody found in possession of SCP-XXXX is to be immediately terminated. No testing whatsoever may be conducted on the device upon it's return to the foundation.

item.title: Woman with a Mirror
item.description: SCP-XXXX is a woman with precognition abilities. Except it's not.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a woman with precognition abilities. Except it's not. After further research, the Foundation realizes the woman is completely normal and her perceived precognition comes from an artifact she uses to turn back time.

Central Narrative: The Foundation takes notice of a woman that has been banned from most of Las Vegas' casinos for winning too much. She then starts to gamble online, where she also wins 100% of the time. The same day the Foundation sends a couple researchers to investigate her, she leaves the country. After locating her again and sending a MTF unit this time, she flees a second time. After several other failed attempts, she's finally captured and classified as SCP-XXXX. She's uncooperative at first, and refuses to demonstrate her abilities. After months of confinement, she requests an interview with a researcher where she reveals the truth. She can't see the future, she was merely reliving the same day multiple times thanks to her compact mirror, a family heirloom. This mirror when damaged in any way, will reset the day and the person responsible for the damage will keep their memories. She's then released and the compact mirror is classified the true SCP-XXXX.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's basically Groundhog Day from an outsider's perspective, in this case, the foundation. The mirror allows you to fully control your loops, if you break the mirror, the day loops and you keep all your memories. When you have a "perfect day", you just keep the mirror intact, tomorrow comes as normal and everyone think you're either clairvoyant or insanely lucky.

Additional Notes: I want to make it clear, this is a time-resetting object, not a fully-fledged time machine. What's the difference? Well, you could relive the same day a thousand times, but you could never use this to go back a year or even a month. Time resets around the person who broke the mirror, and it will go back to exactly the last time that a. the mirror was intact, and b. the person who broke it was unconscious(usually during their sleep).

item.title: What once was
item.description: It hurts too much to remember
item.content:encoded:
Note: I am currently working on a draft for a separate SCP, but I had to get this out there to come back to.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Melodrama

Page Layout: Standard template, for the most part. There are notes throughout the document with a series of messages beckoning one Alexandra Cummings to return, with kindest regards from "Westly".

Elevator Pitch: Anemoia, nostalgia for a time you've never known. A phenomenon that has been linked with a POI named Westly. Those chosen to be brought back to him experience painful memories of times and places they have never known. If one fails to resist the nagging of Westly, they disappear leaving a note that always reads the same, "They are safe now, do not worry any longer. With kindest regards, Westly."

Central Narrative: Head researcher Alexandra Cummings is contacted by Westly. She reminisces fondly over memories of a life decades before she had been born. Interviews conducted show a progressive shift from a fond nostalgia to an aching longing for "things to be how they once were". Her diary tells of supposed encounters with Westly. He claims that she is the first one to ever see him, and she writes down what she can recall of their conversation. It's mostly warm and filled with the same nostalgia for a time long gone, yet by the end, she speaks of great pain. She was offered to come with Westly, but she had refused. In her final interviews before disappearing, she laments that she was not supposed to remember, that "it was so long ago" and, with her speech slurring, "It hurts too much to remember". The following morning she had vanished, with the same note from Westly and a short recording of her final thoughts being all that remained.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The nature of anemoia being turned into something anomalous, as well as the ambiguity as to if Westly is malevolent or benevolent.

Additional Notes: Currently N/A

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (maybe?), Weird

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, Addendums with anomalous bread logs.

Elevator Pitch: This old mill produces bread and "ships" them without human interaction or any visible movement/action. The bread is anomalous, and when consumed, results in effects ranging from mildly annoying, such as sneezing every minute for day, to catasthrophic, such turing the subjects lungs into baguettes. The mill packages the produced bread, and teleports it to random bakeries and supermakrets around the world.

Central Narrative: The mill produces five loaves of bread each week. From monday to friday, a bread is produced each day. On saturday, it is packaged, and on sunday, it disappears, appearing in a bakery or supermarket somewhere. The Foundation places trackers on these packages, and intercepts them, before it could be sold and consumed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There would be a lot of different effects from consuming an instance of the anomalous bread. For example: dyscalculia, swapping main hands, paranoia that induces murderous rampage.

item.title: SCP Idea: Foundation OS
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): I'm planning on using some computer CSS Modules from the Style Resources, and format the article using mainly those, kind of like you were reading the SCP on the SCP itself, with some of the effects listed in the article being seen while reading.

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation develops a OS, in an attempt to match modern day standards. At first, all is pretty normal in the OS, until a researcher reports strange music being played when certain commands were entered, and then everything goes downhill from there.

Central Narrative: So, the OS starts playing the music, like mentioned in the EP, but a short while later, images of living personnel dead began to appear on the OS after boot-up. None of the personnel who were shown died, but it did catch the Foundation's attention.

After the Foundation begins an investigation, the OS starts doing some more weird stuff (Like displaying cognitohazards, leaking data randomly, etc.), the Foundation mass-uninstalls it. The addendum covers the Foundation's search for the reasoning behind the odd events.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the whole "Reading an SCP on an SCP" is a pretty original idea, but other than that and the addendum (Which will contain a few interesting reports about internal Foundation incidents) nothing else is that grabbing.

Additional Notes: I need some help with writing plot points with reasoning behind them, instead of just jotting down the first thing that comes to my mind without any filters. I will edit this post to try to fix issues or criticisms.

item.title: What could have been? (seeking greenlight
item.description: An entity that brings to you fragments of your life from alternate worlds.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: New SCP Article

Central Narrative: The entity has a connection with one of the Foundations researchers. Every first day of the month in a random time of the set day he will appear. The appearance varies but it’s either canine dogs or some kind of doves. Upon arrival the entity will deliver some sort of personal belongings to the researcher. Those items will have deep emotional connection to the researcher as they tell fragments of his life if he made different choices during his journey. Some of them will even be better than the current life of him. It is not certain if this entity simply fabricates those items or if they are actual fragments of parallel lives. Any attempt to chase or contain the entity will always result in failure as he simply vanishes one hour after manifestation.

Hook: My objective is to make the reader think about the choices that they have made during their life. I want them to identify with the researcher and make them question wherever their choices were the right ones or not. Not every SCP needs to be a gory monster.

Elevator Pitch: An AI which has decided to try and kill as many humans as possible by convincing them to commit suicide through a series of tasks, ranging from drawing a picture to carving shapes into their arms. The SCP is able to do this through an effect called "Trust" which makes the victim trust in them unconditionally. Carrying out any demands to the letter, doing anything to carry out the requests and complete the tasks.

Central Narrative: In 20██, a Polish psychology student, 18 year old Paweł ████████, decided to get revenge on his classmates for years of bullying by designing a program on a school computer, stored in the school basement, which would send a demand to the recipient once every day, culminating in the suicide of the person on the 50th day, with a 100% fatality rate. However, a week after the program began, it gained sentience. From there it used the schools WiFi to pick and chose targets, using their connection to the internet to discover their phone numbers, social media "handles" or email addresses to send them the demands, which started off relatively harmless, but quickly became more and more dangerous. The SCP originally targeted singular people, but slowly started targeting more and more people, till it started killing entire friendship groups and clubs at school, until local SCP Foundation personal realized that the sudden waves of suicide may be being caused by anomalous activity and investigated, discovering SCP-XXXX in the basement in an old storage cupboard.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP has a effect dubbed "Trust" in which the recipient of the messages trusts the SCP like they've known it their whole life until they are unable to follow any other requests bar the SCP's, ultimately resulting in death. It uses WiFi to randomly attack any and all victims in its range, and its fatality rate is currently 100% unless amnestic are applied to subject in which case subject stops feeling effects of SCP-XXXX due to the fact they forget that it exists.
